gaps.sentence: I do not know whose coat this is — it ___ belong to one of the guests.
gaps.explanation: 'Might' hedges a guess when the speaker is not sure: might belong.

gaps.sentence: Students ___ to hand in essays by Friday at the latest.
gaps.hint: ought to takes the full infinitive
gaps.explanation: 'Ought to' takes the full infinitive, so only 'ought' fits before 'to': ought.

gaps.sentence: She ___ have brought a present, but it was kind of her anyway.
gaps.explanation: 'Needn't have' plus the participle means the action happened but was unnecessary: needn't have brought.

gaps.sentence: I ___ rather not comment until the investigation is over.
gaps.hint: a polite refusal with would rather not
gaps.explanation: 'Would rather not' declines politely: would rather not.

gaps.sentence: You ___ better not be late again; the boss is getting tired of it.
gaps.explanation: The negative of 'had better' places 'not' after 'better': had better not be.

gaps.sentence: The report ___ to be submitted by noon tomorrow.
gaps.explanation: 'Has to' expresses obligation with a third-person subject: has to be.

gaps.sentence: Library books ___ be taken out of the reading room.
gaps.hint: a passive prohibition with mustn't be
gaps.explanation: Prohibitions can be passive: mustn't be taken.

gaps.sentence: It was careless of her — she ___ have prepared more thoroughly for the interview.
gaps.explanation: 'Should have' criticizes a failure to act properly: should have prepared.
